memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The 100 talents of silver were used to cast the bases for the sanctuary and for the curtain - 100 bases from the 100 talents, one talent for each base. They used the 1,775 shekels to make the hooks for the posts, to overlay the tops of the posts, and to make their bands." - Exod 38:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is where the redemption money went. Every one of those half-shekels was melted together and cast into the bases that the entire tabernacle stood on.

One hundred talents, one hundred bases, one talent each. The whole structure rested on silver that represented ransomed lives.

Nothing in God's dwelling place stood on anything else.

That is a picture worth carrying. The Christian life does not rest on our performance, our feelings, our consistency or our usefulness. It rests entirely on redemption already paid. No one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ (1 Cor 3:11).

And notice where the foundations were: in the ground, out of sight, under everything. Nobody in the camp ever saw those silver bases. But every frame, every curtain, every beautiful thing rested on them.

The most important thing about your life is something invisible — whether it is standing on Christ.

The leftover silver became the hooks and bands on the posts, so redemption was visible above ground as well. Buried below, gleaming above. Redemption from bottom to top.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is your life actually resting on?
2. Do you find yourself trying to add to Christ's finished work?
3. How would today feel different if you truly believed the foundation is already laid?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my life rests on Your redemption alone. Keep me standing there and nowhere else. Amen.
